headline: DMP banned weapons and firecrackers for Ashura processions in Dhaka
summary: The restriction covers swords, spears, and fireworks to ensure public safety and maintain the religious solemnity of the mourning marches.
details: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has prohibited the carrying of weapons and weapon-like items, as well as the use of fireworks and firecrackers, during Ashura processions in the capital on June 26.

caption:
No swords or firecrackers in Dhaka's Ashura processions this year.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has prohibited the carrying of weapons and weapon-like items, as well as the use of fireworks and firecrackers, during Ashura processions in the capital on June 26.

A public notice issued by Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed under sections 28 and 29 of the DMP Ordinance prohibits the use of cleavers, daggers, spears, lances, swords, and sticks.

The DMP stated that in previous years, some participants had carried weapons, which created untoward situations that threatened public safety and caused panic among citizens.

Additionally, the police force noted that while lighting fireworks and firecrackers has become a custom, it does not align with the religious solemnity of the day of mourning.

Ashura, observed on the 10th of Muharram, commemorates the martyrdom of Imam Hussain, the grandson of Prophet Muhammad, at the Battle of Karbala in 680 CE.

Tazia processions are mourning marches held by Shia Muslims to remember this tragedy.
